prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B027 is the one case where all six of us independently placed the same candidate first, but I do not treat that unanimity as the argument. The scientific case is a complete chain from mechanism to patient. Holst established the incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion in humans, Mojsov identified the biologically active GLP-1(7-36)/(7-37) peptide forms, and Drucker defined receptor action, the wider proglucagon-derived biology and the route to therapy. This produced a drug class with very large randomized outcome trials, now showing benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal risk. Confirmation is independent and extensive, the interpretation is stable, and the timing is ripe. A single-achievement prize also gives a clean physiological citation that fits the Physiology or Medicine mandate better than most competitors do.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The three-name cap forces the exclusion of Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose long-acting analogue engineering (liraglutide, semaglutide) is what delivered the clinical impact, and the supplied credit list omits other early peptide contributors, such as Habener, whom I recall. A prize for physiology that leaves out the drug developers may look incomplete, while one that includes them dilutes the basic-science logic. There is also a real risk that the committee rewards sheer commercial and clinical visibility rather than the originality of the discovery, and Mojsov's priority relative to others has been disputed in ways I cannot settle from the supplied materials.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks B027 first but proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Knudsen's engineering of long-acting analogues as the translational step that made the discovery matter and Mojsov's peptide work as real but secondary.
responses.response: I take the point that without semaglutide and liraglutide the physiology would not have changed practice, and I agree Knudsen is a serious claimant. But the Nobel Prize rewards the discovery, and the mechanism-defining step that makes the therapy conceivable is identification of the active peptide. Without Mojsov's work, the pharmacological engineering has no defined target. Drucker and Holst are common to both our trios. The disagreement is only the third seat, and I would put it as physiology and peptide identity versus pharmaceutical optimization. I would not object to Knudsen if the committee defines the achievement as incretin-based therapy rather than GLP-1 physiology, but then the citation should say so, and Habener's absence would become harder to defend.

responses.point: Sandberg places cGAS-STING (B020) second, as a clean two-person mechanism (Chen and Barber) that unified antiviral defense, autoimmunity and cancer immunity, with mature mechanistic confirmation.
responses.response: I rank B020 eighth, and our difference is mainly about maturity. The Chen and Barber attribution is indeed cleaner than most on this list, and the mechanism is not in doubt. But the therapeutic validation is still pending, and I do not see yet what STING agonists or inhibitors have done for patients. I would not say it is wrong, only that the case is mechanism-rich and consequence-poor compared with B027 or B025. I also would want to understand the Ishikawa, Sun and Wu claims, and the cyclic dinucleotide precedent from Vance and Burdette, before treating the two-person configuration as final. If the committee values conceptual clarity over clinical consequence, your case is stronger than I credit, and B020 is a legitimate later-year prize.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks CAR-T (B025) second and optogenetics (B035) third, and also puts SMN2 antisense therapy (B015) fourth, favoring candidates with strong originality and demonstrated clinical effect.
responses.response: We agree on B027 and largely on the identity of the next two. Where I differ is the order and the weight I give to the attribution problems. CAR-T has the stronger clinical record, but the foundational chimeric receptor concept (Eshhar) is outside the credited names, so the configuration is imperfect as listed. For optogenetics, the three-name cap forces painful exclusions (Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck), but the channelrhodopsin identification by Nagel and Hegemann and neuronal deployment by Deisseroth form a coherent core. I rank B035 above B025 because of the originality and breadth of its use across physiology, though I accept it is a method and the clinical translation is still early, so I put them close. I place B015 below these because the nusinersen story depends on drug development within a limited disease area.

responses.point: Perlmann treats orexin/hypocretin (B004) as third, a rare case in which a basic neuropeptide discovery gave a direct disease mechanism in narcolepsy and a drug class, and considers B027 the most basic-science-aligned trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.
responses.response: I share his reading of the B027 trio, which is the configuration I propose. On B004, I agree that the mechanism-to-disease logic is attractive and unusually clear, particularly the link between orexin loss and narcolepsy type 1. My reservation is that independent discovery by de Lecea and Kilduff plus the Yanagisawa and Sakurai orexin work makes any three-person set contestable, and the autoimmune etiology of human narcolepsy remains incompletely resolved. I rank it lower than he does for that reason. It is a strong candidate for a future year, but I would not combine it with B027, because a two-part prize would force the GLP-1 trio to shrink.

uncertainties: Whether the committee defines the achievement as GLP-1 physiology or as incretin-based therapy decides whether Mojsov or Knudsen takes the third seat.
The role of Habener and other early peptide contributors outside the supplied credit list is unresolved, and I have not verified the priority claims.
Whether a two-part prize (for example B027 with B035) is worth the cost of reducing the GLP-1 trio to two names is unclear; I lean against it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B027. My profile documents a co-authored 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann (a committee colleague) and work with Grillner and Ernfors, but none involves the GLP-1 candidate. I have no documented tie to any listed credited name for B027, B035 or B025.
